title: FTC and 20 States Sue Dollar General Over Alleged Checkout Price Overcharges
snippet: Federal regulators and state attorneys general allege the discount giant repeatedly charged higher prices at checkout than advertised on store shelves, capitalizing on low-income shoppers.
content:
Federal regulators and a coalition of 20 states launched a major legal battle against Dollar General on Monday, alleging the discount retail giant has systematically overcharged customers at checkout for years.

According to a lawsuit filed by the Federal Trade Commission (FTC), the company routinely advertised lower prices on store shelves and promotional fliers, only to ring up higher amounts at the register. The agency claims Dollar General generated millions of dollars in additional revenue through these deceptive pricing practices, directly harming low-income households that rely on the chain for affordable essentials.

A History of Overcharging and Ignored Warnings

Regulators assert that the company's executive leadership was well aware of the widespread pricing discrepancies but failed to take corrective action. The complaint details tens of thousands of consumer complaints, a trail of failed state inspections, and covert undercover investigations conducted by FTC agents.

"Dollar General has, for years, repeatedly mislabeled prices, overcharged consumers and failed to correct the issue despite extensive corporate knowledge of the problem," the FTC and state prosecutors said in a joint statement.

Wall Street Reacts as Legal Troubles Mount

This federal lawsuit marks a major escalation in regulatory scrutiny for the discount retailer. Since 2019, Dollar General has already paid out $6 million to settle pricing accuracy enforcement actions across six states. The new coalition suing the chain includes California, Florida, Illinois, Michigan, North Carolina, Ohio, and Tennessee, among others.

Investors reacted swiftly to the legal action, sending Dollar General stock down more than 4% during Monday afternoon trading. Corporate representatives for the retailer did not immediately return requests for comment regarding the lawsuit.
